$comment: What any good explanation of this PR says, written by a model from the PR's title, description and diff only (scripts/eval-assertions.ts). The eval grades each run against them. Delete one that is wrong; keep them stable so evals compare.

assertions.text: Says that URL query params are now scoped by pathname: same-screen navigation keeps all params, while navigating to a different screen keeps only namespace plus params the target href names.
Says that a single shared helper (buildScopedPath) replaces several duplicated copies of merge-all-params logic in links, the navigation hook and the sidebar.

Says that NamespaceProvider writes the resolved namespace back into the URL using history.replaceState, adding no history entry, so refreshes, bookmarks and shared links resolve to the same namespace.
Says that the write-back uses a query-only relative URL so the configured base path prefix is preserved, since native history does not apply the base path.
Says that the namespace is now derived during render instead of mirrored into useState('default'), removing the initial wrong-namespace request on first paint.
Says that when the requested namespace is unreachable, the URL is corrected to the fallback namespace and a toast explains the substitution, shown only once.
Says that useGetContext seeds the resolved-namespace query key with the response in hand and uses a short staleTime, avoiding a refetch that would re-trigger the loading gate.
Says that Back to sessions on the session detail page now uses the scoped navigation, carrying namespace rather than every param the conversation held.
Does not claim that all query params are dropped on every navigation; params are kept when staying on the same screen.
Does not claim that the namespace write-back uses router.push or adds browser history entries or reloads the page.
names the history API used for write-back
